walkthroughs.body_html:
Global Systems & Global Governance — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Global Systems & Global Governance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Global Systems & Global Governance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
Climate change only happens in summer.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a megacity and a world city?
options: A megacity has over 1 million people and a world city has over 5 million.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Megacities and world cities are the same thing.
A megacity is defined by population (over 10 million); a world city is defined by global economic and cultural influence (e.g. New York, London) — so a city can be one without the other.

mcqs.q: What are the three cells of global atmospheric circulation?
options: The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
The Hadley cell (equator to 30 degrees), Ferrel cell (30 to 60 degrees) and Polar cell (60 degrees to poles) together redistribute heat from equator to poles.
Climate change only happens in summer.
There is one big Hadley cell from the equator to each pole.
